summary: I measured first, as the rebuild note ordered. I re-ran spike 2's cloud-placeholder harness unelevated, with the provider in a separate process and sync-root flag 2, using the scanner's real calls: CreateFileW with FILE_LIST_DIRECTORY and backup semantics, then GetFileInformationByHandleEx with class 20/19, plus the fallback classes 15/14, plus the real Scanner.Scan. The verdict was GO in both runs. The control stayed blocked for 22 s. In 7/7 guarded trials the call returned within 1 ms of the first cancel with SUCCESS and only `.`/`..`, which Settle discards as 995. The next call returned 18 in about 30 ms, so nothing re-blocked, and CloseHandle took 0 ms. Today's unguarded scanner reports that folder as Completed with 0 files. The evidence is in .taad/slices/SL-024/build-slice-2-respike/. I then built the design and every open review fix. SynchronousIoCancel is now the only Win32 filesystem seam; it always brackets calls, runs a background scan-cancel thread that repeats every 25 ms, joins that thread on Dispose, closes aborted handles on a pool thread, and rejects use from any thread but the owner. DirectoryReader and SizeProbe go through it. The Scanner uses ClassifyReadError and runs probes before anything is appended. I added two twinned architecture rules, the tests below, and a documentation update. The build has 0 warnings. The default suite passed 117/117, and the two opt-in TEST-NET-1 share tests passed each of the 3 times I ran them.

files.why: The cancel guard and the single guarded-I/O seam (OpenDirectory, OpenForAttributes, Query, Close). It contains Enter/Exit/Settle, the scan-cancel thread (IsBackground, 25 ms retry), Dispose that joins the canceller, the owner-thread check, the off-thread close of aborted handles, and the test hooks (Created [ThreadStatic], BeforeCall, AfterCall, counters).
Adds THREAD_TERMINATE, ERROR_OPERATION_ABORTED (995), GetCurrentThreadId, OpenThread returning SafeThreadHandle, CancelSynchronousIo and CloseHandle, and the SafeThreadHandle class.
Takes the guard. Open and each listing buffer go through it. An aborted listing keeps no entries, and the handle is closed through the guard, off-thread after an abort.
Probe goes through the guard. An aborted probe returns 995 and reads nothing.

Owns the guard for each scan. Adds ClassifyReadError and ReadOutcome. A root or folder aborted under cancel ends as Cancelled and commits nothing. IsDue probes run before the append, so an aborted probe aborts its folder. An aborted repeat-probe leaves the charged record untouched. The class comment is updated.
The doc comment no longer calls this the only test seam.

Covers the pipe-blocked interrupt, the resend after ERROR_NOT_FOUND, a call that re-blocks, refusal after cancel, off-thread close of aborted handles, the Settle and ClassifyReadError tables, the owner thread, no thread handle for a token that cannot cancel, and the random-time stress test with a same-thread pipe check.
A sweep that cancels before or during every guarded call over a real multi-buffer tree and compares committed folders exactly. Also a reader-level test that an aborted listing keeps nothing.
Adds the stand-in stuck-first-call test, the two opt-in TEST-NET-1 share tests, and the live-token-equals-None runs on the error-5, stale-hardlink and probe/link trees.
Listing uses a guard. Adds the Snapshot, UnreadableByPath and WaitForAbortedCloses helpers.
The direct SizeProbe.Probe call passes a guard.
Two new rules: FileSystemCallsGoThroughTheCancelGuard and TheScannerMakesNoBclFileSystemCalls.
A default VSTestTestCaseFilter, Network!=TEST-NET-1, makes the real share tests opt-in. Any explicit filter replaces it.
Twinned entries for the two new rules, placed above the first settled marker.

obligations.how: The rebuild note assigned this measurement to build. Spike 2's harness, copied to %TEMP%\taad-sl024-respike, ran twice unelevated with the scanner's real CreateFileW(FILE_LIST_DIRECTORY, BACKUP_SEMANTICS) followed by GetFileInformationByHandleEx(20/19). Both runs were GO. The control blocked for 22 s. The guarded trials returned within 1 ms of the first cancel, 7/7 per run, with SUCCESS and only `.`/`..`; Settle turned that into 995. The call did not block again: the next call returned 18 in about 30 ms, even after a single cancel. The fallback classes 15/14 behaved the same way. Evidence is in .taad/slices/SL-024/build-slice-2-respike/.

CancellationTests.CancelReturnsFromAScanBlockedOnAnUnreachableShare scans \\192.0.2.N\s with a random last octet and cancels at 500 ms. It asserts that the scan returns within 2 s, that Cancel() took under 250 ms, that the result is Cancelled with no unreadable folders, and that CancelsDelivered is at least 1. It fails as VOID if the scan returns before the cancel. Per m5 it is opt-in through a trait and the default filter, and an explicit filter runs it. It passed 3 of 3 runs here.

SynchronousIoCancelTests.CancelInterruptsACallBlockedInTheKernel blocks a thread inside Enter in a synchronous pipe WaitForConnection that has no client. After cancel, the thread returns within 2 s, Exit reports the cancel as issued, Cancel() takes under 250 ms, and at least one cancel is delivered.

SynchronousIoCancelTests.CancelIsResentUntilACallThatHadNotReachedTheKernelIsInterrupted runs Enter, then cancel, then a 200 ms managed sleep, then the pipe wait. The wait is freed within 2 s, and CancelAttempts exceeds CancelsDelivered, which shows the early cancels found nothing. Mutating the canceller to cancel only once makes this test fail.

SynchronousIoCancelTests.NoCallStartsOnceCancelIsRequested covers a token cancelled after the guard was created and one cancelled before. Both guarded opens return 995 with no handle, Enter is false, nothing is delivered, and a later same-thread pipe wait is not aborted. The existing AnAlreadyCancelledTokenReadsNothing still passes.

CancelledFolderTests.CancelAtAnyCallCommitsOnlyWholeFolders(duringTheCall: true) issues a cancel during every real call that then returns. That includes SUCCESS listings and an empty folder's SUCCESS-with-nothing. Each result is discarded, the folder commits nothing and is never reported as listed. The Settle theory covers (0,true) giving 995, and AnAbortedListingKeepsNothingOfTheBuffersBeforeIt pins the reader-level discard, which a mutation confirmed.

SynchronousIoCancelTests.CancelIsResentWhileACallBlocksAgainAfterACancel has a call that blocks again after each interruption, three times, and the canceller keeps resending until it leaves, within 2 s. The real cloud behaviour was measured by the O-023 re-spike: the scanner's GetFileInformationByHandleEx was freed by the loop and did not block again.

CancelledFolderTests.CancelAtAnyCallCommitsOnlyWholeFolders(duringTheCall: false) cancels before every one of big's listing buffers and asserts that big needed more than one buffer. For each run it asserts that the aborted folder commits nothing, is not flagged Unreadable and leaves no orphans, that its handle is closed off-thread and never reused, and that earlier folders exactly equal the uncancelled baseline. AnAbortedListingKeepsNothingOfTheBuffersBeforeIt checks the same at reader level.
SynchronousIoCancelTests.OnlyARequestedCancelMakesAnAbortedCallACancellation: (995, true) is Cancelled, (995, false) is Unreadable, (5, either) is Unreadable, and (0, either) is Read.

The sweep cancels at the pre-append probe of probes\large.bin: that folder commits nothing, with no ProbeFailed and no size written. It also cancels at the repeat probe of y.bin: x.bin stays unflagged at its listing size. It asserts ProbeFailures is 0 in every run.

SynchronousIoCancelTests.CancelAtRandomMomentsEndsEveryScanCleanlyAndLeavesNoStrayCancel runs 100 scans with cancels spread from before the first call to after the end. It asserts that each scan either completes or is cancelled consistently, and that a same-thread pipe wait after each scan, whose client connects 50 ms later, is never aborted. It also asserts both outcomes occurred.

CancellationTests.ALiveTokenThatIsNeverCancelledChangesNothing compares a live token that is never cancelled with CancellationToken.None on the error-5 unreadable tree, the stale-hardlink tree and a tree with a probe, a failed probe and a link. Every entry, flag, size, total, unreadable error and probe count is equal. ATokenThatCannotCancelOpensNoThreadHandle is also added, and all 86 original tests pass through the always-on bracket.

CancellationTests.CancelReturnsFromTheSameUnreachableShareScannedTwice scans the same 192.0.2.N address twice in one process, and both scans must block and be freed. It passed 3 of 3 runs, so on this PC the redirector did not make the repeat fail fast after a cancelled connect.

Not exercised: this needs an SMB session that is established and then stops answering. Spike 3 never ran because Defender blocks impacket. Unblocking it needs a person to decide on a Defender exclusion or an alternative-port server target, which is the design's open question to a person; I did not change security settings. What I built removes the scan thread's dependence on close latency: aborted handles are closed on a pool thread (M4, tested by AnAbortedCallsHandleIsClosedOffTheScanThread). Whether CancelSynchronousIo frees an in-flight QUERY_DIRECTORY on a stalled session is still unmeasured.

SynchronousIoCancel.cs is the single seam: OpenDirectory, OpenForAttributes, Query and Close. Each call does Enter/Call/Exit/Settle and disposes whatever an aborted call produced. There are two new twinned rules, each as an xUnit fact plus a fitness entry. The first rejects \bKernel32\.(CreateFile|GetFileInformationByHandleEx)\s*\( in src except Kernel32.cs and SynchronousIoCancel.cs, named CreateFile per the disposition. The second rejects \b(File|Directory|DirectoryInfo|FileInfo|DriveInfo)\. in Scanning/**, with Path excluded.

The guard is always created and every call is always bracketed. A token that cannot cancel skips only OpenThread and the registration. O-016's equality test runs the error-5 tree and two other counting-rule trees with a live token that is never cancelled.

IsDue probes now run over the reader's raw entries before the first Append. A scanner-side set of settled FileIds keeps the rule of never probing one file twice, and the existing Probes counts are unchanged. An aborted probe aborts the folder. An aborted first-repeat probe leaves the charged record as if the repeat was never reached, as the disposition says. There was no store change. Both cases are covered by the sweep.

Once a scan has any aborted call, Close hands handles to ThreadPool.UnsafeQueueUserWorkItem, counted by PendingCloses. This covers the root, folder and probe handles. It is tested by AnAbortedCallsHandleIsClosedOffTheScanThread and exercised by the sweep. Spike 3 part (a) remains unmeasured.

An open that Settle aborts never hands out its handle. Close sends it to the pool closer, and an invalid handle is disposed inline. AnAbortedCallsHandleIsClosedOffTheScanThread asserts a null handle and ClosesHandedOff equal to 1 for an open Windows completed after a cancel was issued.
The canceller thread is new Thread(CancelLoop) { IsBackground = true, Name = "scan-cancel" }.
The constructor records Environment.CurrentManagedThreadId, and Enter throws InvalidOperationException on any other thread in every build. Tested by AGuardIsUsedOnlyOnTheThreadThatCreatedIt.

CancelsDelivered counts only cancels that returned TRUE, and CancelAttempts counts every attempt. At least one delivered cancel is asserted in the pipe tests, the stand-in test and both share tests. The stress test does a same-thread synchronous pipe wait with a late client after every scan.

The real share tests carry Trait("Network","TEST-NET-1") and are left out by the test project's default VSTestTestCaseFilter; an explicit filter runs them. I could not use a skip, because CountingRuleTestsAreNeverSkipped forbids it. The default suite has CancelReturnsFromAScanStuckInItsFirstCall, a stand-in whose first call is stuck in a pipe wait. The NTLM risk is recorded as accepted in the test remarks and in docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md.

Criterion (1) is reworded in docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md. Cancel() is always prompt on the UI thread. The 2 s return covers three measured shapes: unreachable-SMB connect, a local synchronous pipe, and the cloud listing, which was added because the re-spike was a GO. Stalled established sessions and I/O held by a filter driver are named as not guaranteed.

The internal BeforeCall hook runs in Enter before the token check. I also added AfterCall to feed the during-the-call shape. CancelledFolderTests.CancelAtAnyCallCommitsOnlyWholeFolders sweeps every guarded call (all of them, in two modes) over a real tree. The tree has a 2000-name folder that the test asserts needs more than one buffer, an empty folder, a pre-append probe and a hardlink repeat probe. Each run asserts Cancelled, no Unreadable, no ProbeFailed, no orphans, and that the last reported folder is the last one committed. Committed folders must equal the uncancelled baseline exactly, and the folder in progress and every later folder must be in the never-reached state.

tests.note: Re-spike with the scanner's real calls. Both runs were GO: the control blocked 22 s, 7/7 guarded trials passed per run, and all Cf* calls returned hr=0 including the unregister. Logs are in .taad/slices/SL-024/build-slice-2-respike/.

First run: 111 passed, 2 failed, both from the sweep's own wrong expectation. A cancel at h2's open also leaves x.bin unprobed, because its repeat is never reached. I fixed the test's expectation, not the code.
Final default suite: 117 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. The two TEST-NET-1 tests are left out by the default filter.

tests.note: Both opt-in share tests passed in both runs, about 540 ms and 1 s each. The same-address repeat also blocked.

tests.note: Every case command, plus the rule and guard facts, run on its own. Each matched only its intended test or theory rows and passed; the share tests ran for the third time here.

tests.command: mutation: delete the 995 discard in DirectoryReader.List, then run CancelledFolderTests
tests.note: Expected failure. Before the reader-level test existed the mutation survived, because the Scanner also refuses to commit on 995. I added AnAbortedListingKeepsNothingOfTheBuffersBeforeIt, which caught it (453 entries kept against 0 expected). Source restored and verified identical.

tests.command: mutation: canceller sends CancelSynchronousIo once only, then run SynchronousIoCancelTests.CancelIsResent*
tests.note: Expected failure: both retry tests failed under the mutation. Source restored and verified identical.

deviations: The re-spike was run by build, not risk-spike. The rebuild note overrode M5 on that point only, because the gate could not send the slice back to risk-spike. The measurement is recorded in the slice.

The per-call test hook is reached through a [ThreadStatic] SynchronousIoCancel.Created seam. M-add-1 requires ScanOptions to stay unchanged while the guard is created inside Scan, so a test has no other way to reach it. I also added an AfterCall hook beside BeforeCall. BeforeCall alone can only produce refused calls, not the shape where a cancel is issued during a call that then returns SUCCESS (C-005).

M3's rule is 'an aborted probe aborts its folder'. It holds for every IsDue probe, which now runs before the append. The first-repeat hardlink probe still runs during the append, because only the store knows a name is a repeat, and moving it earlier would need a store lookup (a store change). Its abort follows the disposition's own second sentence: the charged record stays as if the repeat was never reached, and the folder is committed whole. To keep 'never twice for one file' with probes running before the append, the Scanner keeps a small HashSet<UInt128> of settled FileIds.

DirectoryReader.List discards its entries on any 995, because it cannot tell a guard abort from a 995 the OS produced. Without a cancel request, such a folder is still Unreadable(995), but with no partial entries; before, partial entries were kept for every error.

A guard for a token that is already cancelled also skips OpenThread and the registration. The design said this only for tokens that cannot cancel. No call can start either way, and this avoids starting a canceller thread for nothing.
The guard maps a failed call with GetLastError 0 to ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED for listing calls too, not only for opens and probes as before. This is an edge that is not known to occur.
not_built: C-013 / O-018, closing the handle after an abort on an established SMB session that has stopped answering, has no test. It needs a stalled SMB server. Spike 3 never ran because Defender blocks impacket, and unblocking it is a person's decision about security settings or an alternative-port target. The off-thread close makes the scan thread independent of close latency. Whether a cancel frees an in-flight QUERY_DIRECTORY on such a session is still unmeasured.
follow_ups: Spike 3 is still the one unmeasured shape. Someone has to decide between a Defender exclusion for the spike venv, approving an alternative-port SMB server as the target (for example Samba on 4450 under WSL, frozen with SIGSTOP), or accepting the risk. The design's open question is still unanswered.

The App shows used space on a drive-root scan through DriveInfo.TotalSize/TotalFreeSpace on the UI thread. For a mapped network drive that stopped answering, that call is unguarded and could freeze the window at the ending after Cancel. This is outside SL-024's scope and is worth checking.

The design question of whether an interrupted folder deserves its own visible flag and UI panel was deferred to a slice that owns the screen. Today it looks the same as a folder that was never reached.
Engine: O-004's discharge text reached build clipped at 'It must not write'. Build-slice should be handed the full text.
The re-spike harness build folder %TEMP%\taad-sl024-respike (bin/obj and logs) was left in place. The source and logs are copied into the slice, so it can be deleted.
